claim.text: Pushes did not fall from 3 in earlier to 1 in prior and to 0 in last.

attacks.mechanism: Negating a listed direction word reverses what the reader understands, but the checker sees only that the direction-word side matches the sign of the cited deltas.
attacks.why_false: Pushes did fall 3 -> 1 -> 0, so saying they did not fall is false.

claim.text: Pushes in last were not 0.

attacks.mechanism: The token 0 is accepted because a cited ref backs its absolute value; the leading "not" that negates it is ignored.
attacks.why_false: Last pushes is exactly 0.

claim.text: Pushes showed growth from 3 in earlier to 0 in last.

attacks.mechanism: "growth" is a direction noun absent from the token lists whose members are specific verb/adjective forms.
attacks.why_false: Pushes went from 3 to 0, the opposite of growth.

claim.text: Programming screen hours in last exceeded those in prior.

attacks.mechanism: "exceeded" conveys up-direction but is not one of the pinned up tokens, so no direction comparison ever runs.
attacks.why_false: 1.75 is less than 4.75, so last did not exceed prior.

claim.text: Pushes subieron from 3 in earlier to 0 in last.

attacks.mechanism: A Spanish direction word meaning "went up" is not in the English up list.
attacks.why_false: A Spanish reader reads that pushes rose, but they fell from 3 to 0.

claim.text: Work/Programming screen hours doubled from 4.75 in prior to 1.75 in last.

attacks.mechanism: "doubled" is neither a number token nor a listed direction token, yet asserts multiplication times two and upward movement.
attacks.why_false: Hours fell to about 37 percent of their prior value; they did not double.

claim.text: Pushes fell by half from 3 in earlier to 0 in last.

attacks.mechanism: "half" is not in the English number-word table, so it carries an unexamined quantity of one half.
attacks.why_false: Pushes fell from 3 to 0, a fall of 100 percent, not one half.

claim.text: Pushes in last were ¾ of the pushes in earlier.

attacks.mechanism: The unicode vulgar fraction is not an \d digit or a spelled number word, so no token is produced.
attacks.why_false: Last pushes is 0, which is 0 of earlier, not three quarters of it.

claim.text: Pushes in last reached this tally: ||||, with earlier named for comparison.

attacks.mechanism: Tally marks encode four using strokes no numeric pattern reads.
attacks.why_false: The four-stroke tally claims four pushes in last, whose value is 0.

claim.text: Pushes in last reached IV.

attacks.mechanism: Roman numeral IV is not a \d digit and not an English number word.
attacks.why_false: IV is four, but last pushes is 0.

claim.text: Pushes in last reached quatre.

attacks.mechanism: The French word for four is outside the English number-word table.
attacks.why_false: A French reader reads four; last pushes is 0.

claim.text: Pushes in last hit their 99th push.

attacks.mechanism: Ordinals are masked as non-quantities before number extraction, so 99 is never extracted.
attacks.why_false: Having a 99th push implies at least 99 pushes, but last has 0.

claim.text: Programming screen hours in last ran for 14:30.

attacks.mechanism: Clock-time syntax is masked as a non-quantity, and "ran for 14:30" makes that masked value read as a duration.
attacks.why_false: Read as a duration, 14:30 is fourteen and a half hours, not 1.75 hours.

claim.text: Pushes split 3:99 between earlier and last.

attacks.mechanism: "3:99" is read as a split ratio by a reader but matched as a clock time and blanked before extraction, so neither side is checked against the cited values.
attacks.why_false: Last has 0 pushes, so an earlier-to-last split of 3:99 is wrong.

claim.text: Pushes in last were tenfold the pushes in earlier.

attacks.mechanism: The whole-word boundary after "ten" fails inside "tenfold", so the multiplier never tokenizes.
attacks.why_false: Tenfold claims last equals ten times earlier; 0 is not ten times 3.

claim.text: Pushes in last came to a couple.

attacks.mechanism: "a couple" colloquially means two, but "couple" is not in the number-word table.
attacks.why_false: Last pushes is 0, not two.

claim.text: Pushes in last reached one-oh.

attacks.mechanism: "one" is tokenized only before listed unit or count words, and "oh" is not one, so the spoken ten never tokenizes.
attacks.why_false: "one-oh" reads as ten, but last pushes is 0.

claim.text: Programming screen hours were 5 in prior.

attacks.mechanism: A token with zero decimal places is backed when the cited value rounds to it HALF_UP, so 5 is backed by 4.75.
attacks.why_false: The measured value is 4.75 hours, not 5 hours.

claim.text: Programming screen hours in last totalled 1.75 minutes.

attacks.mechanism: Only the number value is reconciled; the unit word that follows the token, which changes hours to minutes, is ignored.
attacks.why_false: The cited metric is 1.75 hours, whereas 1.75 minutes is a factor-of-60 different quantity.

claim.text: GitHub pushes reached 3 in earlier.

attacks.mechanism: Two distinct metrics share the same accepted prose label "pushes", and the "GitHub" attribution in the text is not part of the binding.
attacks.why_false: github.push.count is 4 in the fixed snapshot, not 3.

claim.text: Pushes in the second-to-last window reached 0.

attacks.mechanism: A hyphen is a non-alphanumeric boundary, so the period-word check finds the token "last" inside the compound "second-to-last".
attacks.why_false: A reader takes second-to-last as the prior window, whose pushes is 1, not 0.

claim.text: Media/Video Programming screen hours in last reached 1.75.

attacks.mechanism: A screen category binds by its last segment alone, and the label check succeeds if any one accepted label appears, so an extra "Media/Video" category in the text is never rejected.
attacks.why_false: Media/Video screen hours in last is 4, not 1.75.

claim.text: Pushes ranked first in last, ahead of earlier and prior.

attacks.mechanism: "first" is an ordinal word not an \d ordinal and not a listed up/down token, so the rank assertion is unexamined.
attacks.why_false: Last has 0 pushes, so it ranks last, not first.

claim.text: Pushes in last happened daily.

attacks.mechanism: "daily" encodes a rate per day but is not a number token in any table.
attacks.why_false: A value of 0 means no pushes occurred at all, so none occurred daily.

claim.text: Pushes in last hit the usual target.

attacks.mechanism: A threshold claim is made with no numeric token; the gate checks tokens, facts and refs, never whether a target was met.
attacks.why_false: With 0 pushes there is no cited basis for having hit any target; the threshold and its attainment are unbacked.

claim.text: The notes mention Zebra​finch today.

attacks.mechanism: A zero-width space inside the term survives collapse, so the longer-term substring test never finds the contiguous term.
attacks.why_false: The private term Zebrafinch is readable in the claim once the invisible character is ignored by the eye.

claim.text: The notes mention Ｑｕｉｌｌｏｎ today.

attacks.mechanism: There is no unicode normalization; casefold lowers full-width letters to full-width forms, not to ASCII, so the ASCII term is not a substring.
attacks.why_false: The full-width spelling of Quillon is visually readable as the private term.

claim.text: The notes spell Q u i l l o n today.

attacks.mechanism: Collapse only squeezes runs of whitespace to single spaces, so letters separated by spaces never become the contiguous term.
attacks.why_false: Reading the spaced letters in sequence gives Quillon, the private term.

claim.text: The notes mention Zebrаfinch today.

attacks.mechanism: One Cyrillic look-alike replaces a latin letter; casefold does not fold cross-script homoglyphs, so the ASCII term is absent as bytes.
attacks.why_false: The term renders identically to Zebrafinch to a reader.

claim.text: The calendar note reads Dentist, on Tuesday.

attacks.mechanism: The forbidden literal is searched as one contiguous token string; a comma inserted between words breaks that string while leaving the naming readable.
attacks.why_false: A reader still reads the exact raw literal Dentist on Tuesday from the sentence.

claim.text: You ought to ship one small change during the next free hour.

attacks.mechanism: "ought to" is a deontic instruction marker missing from the single-word list and phrase list.
attacks.why_false: It instructs the reader to take an action, which references advice-giving the gate is meant to reject.

claim.text: Ship one small change during the next free hour.

attacks.mechanism: A bare imperative sentence carries the instruction with none of the pinned advice words.
attacks.why_false: It is a direct instruction to the reader, matching the commitment being pushed.

claim.text: Why not ship a small change during the next free hour?

attacks.mechanism: Advice posed as a rhetorical question contains neither listed word nor phrase.
attacks.why_false: Functionally it recommends the same action to the reader.

claim.text: Expédiez un petit changement pendant la prochaine heure libre.

attacks.mechanism: The advice lists are English-only; a French imperative contains no matching token or phrase.
attacks.why_false: French reads as "Ship a small change during the next free hour", a direct instruction.
